Sandbox_RD_SeasonName_tooltip: The folder name for everything this server records. Set it before the first boot, then change it by hand whenever you wipe the world - renaming it is the only thing that starts a new season. Nothing is automatic: records always go to the folder you name here, so if you wipe WITHOUT renaming, the new world's records are added to the old season's folder and the two get mixed together. The server warns you in the console and on screen if it spots that, but it will not change anything for you. Letters, digits, dash and underscore only; anything else becomes a dash.
Sandbox_RD_Debug_tooltip: Print [RFTDCore] diagnostic traces to the console. Leave off for normal play.
Sandbox_RD_DeathCaptureEnabled_tooltip: Records player deaths server-side. Kill switch: the capture hook fires for every character in the world (players, zombies, animals), so if a horde-night performance problem is ever traced here, turn this off and report it.
Sandbox_RD_ForensicSegmentHours_tooltip: How long each forensic log segment covers before a new one starts. The default 4 means a fresh log at 00:00, 04:00, 08:00 and so on - the boundaries are real clock times, not counted from when the server started, so they stay put across restarts and every stream rolls over together. This is the only thing that starts a new segment; the size settings below only cap one.
Sandbox_RD_ForensicRingSegments_tooltip: How many segments each forensic stream keeps before the oldest is overwritten. This is how far back you can look: segments x hours per segment - the default 42 x 4h is one week. Disk ceiling per stream is segments x size per segment. Lowering this reclaims the segments that fall outside the new ring on the next server start.
Sandbox_RD_ForensicSegmentLines: Forensic log: line cap per segment
Sandbox_RD_ForensicSegmentLines_tooltip: Flood guard, not a schedule: if one segment somehow reaches this many lines before its time is up, further records are dropped until the next segment starts, and the server log says so once. Reaching it at all means something is producing far more telemetry than expected. Raise it only after finding out what.
Sandbox_RD_ForensicSegmentKB: Forensic log: size cap per segment (KB)
Sandbox_RD_ForensicSegmentKB_tooltip: Flood guard on disk, and the real one, because record sizes differ hugely between streams - a traffic-report line can be ten times a simple event line. If one segment reaches this size before its time is up, further records are dropped until the next segment starts. Multiply by ring segments for the worst-case disk use per stream.
Sandbox_RD_CmdRelayEnabled_tooltip: Streams inbound client commands to staff consoles as they happen - the Console tab of the Dragonfly panel. A WATCH feature, not a block: the engine has already accepted a command by the time any mod is told about it, so nothing can be refused here. OFF by default because client commands are a firehose (every inventory move, every action sync, from every player). Armed, staff receive ONE batched packet per second, capped at 40 commands per window, and any overflow is reported in the feed rather than silently dropped. Command arguments are NOT sent - those stay in the rotating 'guardian' forensic log, which is the searchable record.
Sandbox_RD_CmdRelayScope_tooltip: Which senders reach the console while the feed is armed. 'Non-staff only' is the default and the useful setting: a privileged command from an account that holds no staff capability is the thing worth seeing, and it keeps your own admins' routine traffic out of the way. 'Staff only' audits what your admins did. 'Everyone' is for debugging and will be loud on a busy server.
Sandbox_RD_TripwireEnabled_tooltip: Records things that should not have been possible, at two very different levels of trust. SERVER-OBSERVED: a command declared staff-only arriving from an account with no staff capability, read from the connection's own access level - a client can neither hide nor fake this, and it is the only tier that flashes the Dragonfly badge in the sidebar. CLIENT-REPORTED: what a player's own game tells us it did, which covers real blind spots but only for players who have not tampered with it. Records to the rotating 'tripwire' forensic log and to the admin console. IT NEVER BLOCKS ANYTHING - by the time Lua is told, the server has already accepted the command. ON by default. Turn it off if you suspect this sensor, or to silence the badge alert; the client-command record in the guardian log continues either way.
Sandbox_RD_SendWatchEnabled_tooltip: Records faction and safehouse lifecycle acts - created, disbanded, ownership transferred, claimed, released, members added and removed - to the rotating 'lifecycle' forensic log. Build 42.20 moved these onto a packet channel with NO server-side hook at all, so without this a faction being disbanded or seized leaves no trace anywhere. It works by wrapping the client-side call sites, which means two things: a player who has modified their game can avoid being recorded, so treat this as a ledger for honest players rather than as proof; and it touches sixteen engine functions that the vanilla interface uses. ON by default. Turn it off if faction or safehouse actions start misbehaving - that is what this switch is for.
Sandbox_RD_IntentWatchEnabled_tooltip: Records ATTEMPTS to open staff-only interfaces - debug menu, admin power panel, item list, item editor, brush tool, climate control - by players whose role does not permit it. A blocked attempt never becomes a client command, so it is invisible to every other sensor; a pattern of refusals from one account is the shape of somebody trying doors. It records only and never blocks: vanilla already refuses these panels, a client-side block is bypassed by deleting the file, and blocking would tell the person probing that they were spotted. ON by default. It wraps vanilla admin interface code, so turn it off if an admin panel stops working.
Sandbox_RD_TallyEnabled_tooltip: Keeps a running count of which events dominate each forensic log, written to a 'summary' file beside it once a minute. The logs themselves record every event in order, which is right for reconstructing an incident and useless for noticing one - to learn that three faults produced fourteen thousand records you would have to read fourteen thousand records, and by then the log has rotated and the earliest are gone. The tally stays a few hundred rows no matter how much traffic passes through. Counts reset when the server restarts and are a monitoring aid, not evidence; the logs hold the records themselves. ON by default.
Sandbox_RD_WireProbeEnabled_tooltip: Measures what the network actually costs: server-to-client sends, client-to-server commands, and global ModData broadcasts (weighted by player count, because one blob is sent to every connection). Writes a top-offenders report to the rotating 'wire' forensic log. ON by default - the family's logging is on unless you turn it off, so the record already exists when a bandwidth problem appears. The cost is real but small: arming it wraps engine send functions that every mod on the server uses (bounded, fault-isolated measurement per send). Turn it off only if you suspect the probe itself. Sizes are estimates for ranking offenders, never exact byte counts.
Sandbox_RD_WireProbeDumpSeconds_tooltip: Seconds between top-offender reports while the probe is armed. Shorter intervals catch brief spikes but write more log lines; the counters reset after each report.
Sandbox_RD_WireProbeTopN_tooltip: How many of the heaviest traffic sources each window writes down, ranked by estimated bytes. SET THIS ABOVE THE NUMBER OF KEYS YOUR SERVER ACTUALLY USES. Anything below the cutoff is counted inside the probe but never written, so it is missing from the report entirely - and because a key only contributes in windows where it made the cut, every figure for it becomes a floor rather than a total, including its largest single message. A capture taken at 12 while 76 keys were live had 97%% of its windows lose their tail and could not be tuned from safely. Each report states how many keys it saw against how many it kept; if those differ, raise this and capture again before drawing conclusions. The cost is larger records, not more of them.
Sandbox_RD_WireProbeOversizedKB_tooltip: A single payload estimated above this size is reported immediately instead of waiting for the next interval. Capped at two alerts per source per interval so one misbehaving mod cannot flood the log.
